hook.en: A farmer, a software engineer, a woman who helps on her family farm without pay, and a student. Which of them are workers in the eyes of an economist?
hook.kn: ರೈತ, ಸಾಫ್ಟ್‌ವೇರ್ ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರ್, ಕುಟುಂಬದ ಹೊಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಬಳವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ದುಡಿಯುವ ಮಹಿಳೆ ಮತ್ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿ. ಅರ್ಥಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಜ್ಞನ ದೃಷ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಇವರಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾರು ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು?

objectives.en: Compare participation of rural and urban, men and women

narration.en: A farmer, a software engineer, a woman who helps on her family farm without pay, and a student. Which of them are workers in the eyes of an economist?
narration.kn: ರೈತ, ಸಾಫ್ಟ್‌ವೇರ್ ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರ್, ಕುಟುಂಬದ ಹೊಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಬಳವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ದುಡಿಯುವ ಮಹಿಳೆ ಮತ್ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿ. ಅರ್ಥಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಜ್ಞನ ದೃಷ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಇವರಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾರು ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು?

body.en: People work to earn a living, and work also gives a sense of self-worth and dignity. Every working person contributes to national income by producing goods and services. All those engaged in economic activities, in whatever capacity, are workers. Those temporarily absent because of illness, injury, bad weather, festivals or social and religious functions are also workers, and so are those who help the main worker in farming or a family business.

points.en: Economic activity = production that adds to GDP
Helpers in family farms and businesses are workers
Temporary absence does not stop one being a worker

narration.en: Anyone engaged in an economic activity that adds to national income is a worker. Even people who help the main earner on the family farm, or who are away for a short time because of illness or festivals, are counted as workers.
narration.kn: ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಆದಾಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸೇರುವ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗಿರುವ ಎಲ್ಲರೂ ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು. ಕುಟುಂಬದ ಹೊಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡುವವರು ಮತ್ತು ಅನಾರೋಗ್ಯದಿಂದ ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕವಾಗಿ ಗೈರಾದವರೂ ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರೇ.

narration.en: Let us build the worker-population ratio on the board, step by step.

say.en: Out of every hundred people, how many are working? That is the worker-population ratio.
We divide the number of workers by the total population and multiply by a hundred.
Picture the population as one long bar. The green part is the workers.
A village has 2,000 people and 760 of them work. The ratio is 38 per cent.
In India the ratio is higher in villages than in towns, and higher for men than for women.

body.en: The worker-population ratio tells us what percentage of the population is actually working. In India it is higher in rural areas than in urban areas, because poor rural families cannot afford to keep members at home, while urban people often study longer and look for jobs that suit their qualifications. Men participate more than women; rural women work more than urban women, since in towns many women do unpaid household work that is not counted as economic activity.

points.en: Higher ratio = more people producing goods and services
Men > women; rural women > urban women

narration.en: The worker-population ratio is the percentage of the population that works. It is higher in villages than in towns and higher for men than for women, because rural families need every earner and much of women's household work is unpaid and not counted.
narration.kn: ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕ-ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಅನುಪಾತವು ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಎಷ್ಟು ಶೇಕಡಾ ಜನರು ದುಡಿಯುತ್ತಾರೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದು ನಗರಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಪ್ರದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮಹಿಳೆಯರಿಗಿಂತ ಪುರುಷರಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು.

caption.en: Move the sliders for a village: the bars show workers and non-workers, and the read-out gives the worker-population ratio.

narration.en: Change the population and the number of workers, and watch the worker-population ratio.

tryThis.en: Population 2,000 and 760 workers: check the ratio is 38%.
Keep workers fixed and raise the population. Why does the ratio fall?
Which is more useful for comparing two villages: the number of workers or the ratio?

caption.en: Households supply labour to firms and receive wages; the goods and services workers produce make up national income.

tryThis.en: Follow the labour arrow from households to firms.
Where do the wages go next?

narration.en: Watch the circular flow. Every worker supplies labour to a firm and is paid for it; what workers produce is the national income.

problem.en: A town has 48,000 people, of whom 16,800 are workers. Of its 20,000 women, 4,200 are workers. Find the worker-population ratio for the town, for women and for men.

answer.en: Town 35%, women 21%, men 45%: men participate far more than women.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A town has 48,000 people, of whom 16,800 are workers. Of its 20,000 women, 4,200 are workers. Find the worker-population ratio for the town, for women and for men.
Class quiz. Discuss, raise hands, and the monitor taps the class answer.
narration.kn: ತರಗತಿ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ, ಕೈ ಎತ್ತಿ, ಮಾನಿಟರ್ ತರಗತಿಯ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಲಿ.

narration.en: CBSE pattern: assertion-reason and case-based questions. Read each carefully.

points.en: A worker is anyone engaged in an economic activity that adds to national income, including helpers on family farms.
points.kn: ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಆದಾಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸೇರುವ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗಿರುವ ಎಲ್ಲರೂ, ಕುಟುಂಬದ ಹೊಲದ ಸಹಾಯಕರೂ ಸೇರಿ, ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು.

points.en: The ratio is higher in rural areas and for men; rural women work more than urban women.
points.kn: ಅನುಪಾತ ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಪ್ರದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪುರುಷರಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು; ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಮಹಿಳೆಯರು ನಗರದ ಮಹಿಳೆಯರಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ದುಡಿಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.

homework.en: Why is the participation of women higher in rural areas than in urban areas?

narration.en: Recap. A worker is anyone engaged in an economic activity that adds to national income, including helpers on family farms. Worker-population ratio = workers ÷ population × 100. The ratio is higher in rural areas and for men; rural women work more than urban women.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಆದಾಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸೇರುವ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗಿರುವ ಎಲ್ಲರೂ, ಕುಟುಂಬದ ಹೊಲದ ಸಹಾಯಕರೂ ಸೇರಿ, ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು. ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕ-ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಅನುಪಾತ = ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು ÷ ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ × 100. ಅನುಪಾತ ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಪ್ರದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪುರುಷರಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು; ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಮಹಿಳೆಯರು ನಗರದ ಮಹಿಳೆಯರಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ದುಡಿಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.
